# Preliminaries {#sec-data}

## Sample

@sec-summary-statistics uses the annual teaching sample of @bali2016, covering U.S. common stocks at each year-end from 1988 through 2012.
The empirical replications use longer monthly samples.

The examples read local Parquet files through `era_pl.load_parquet()`.
The `DATA_DIR` setting points to the data root, and each table lives at `DATA_DIR/schema/table.parquet`.
You can create these files from WRDS with the setup script in @sec-create-data-repository.

### WRDS tables {#sec-data-vintages}

[]{#data-vintages}The table lists the inputs used in this build.
The source update date comes from the metadata embedded in each Parquet file, read with [db2pq](https://iangow.github.io/db2pq/).
It is not the sample end date or the date the file was downloaded.

```{python}
#| echo: false

import re

from db2pq import pq_last_modified
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

tables = [
    ("ff", "factors_monthly", "Fama–French",
     "Monthly factors and the risk-free rate for betas, alphas, and market checks."),
    ("ff", "factors_daily", "Fama–French",
     "Daily market excess returns for the crash checks in @sec-bem7-market and for estimating daily betas."),
    ("crsp", "msf", "CRSP legacy (SIZ)",
     "Legacy prices, shares outstanding, and monthly returns."),
    ("crsp", "dsf", "CRSP legacy (SIZ)",
     "Daily stock returns for beta estimation in @sec-bem-beta."),
    ("crsp", "msenames", "CRSP legacy (SIZ)",
     "Historical share codes, exchanges, and industries."),
    ("comp", "funda", "Compustat",
     "Annual fundamentals for book equity."),
    ("crsp", "ccmxpf_lnkused", "CRSP/Compustat Merged",
     "Historical links from Compustat firms to CRSP securities."),
    ("crsp", "msedelist", "CRSP legacy (SIZ)",
     "Delisting returns and codes for monthly holding-period returns."),
    ("crsp", "msi", "CRSP legacy (SIZ)",
     "CRSP value-weighted index for the market factor comparison."),
]

rows = [
    "| WRDS table | Dataset | Used for | Source updated |",
    "|:---|:---|:---|:---|",
]
for schema, name, dataset, purpose in tables:
    metadata = pq_last_modified(name, schema) or ""
    match = re.search(r"Updated (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", metadata)
    updated = match[1] if match else "Not recorded"
    rows.append(f"| `{schema}.{name}` | {dataset} | {purpose} | {updated} |")

display(Markdown("\n".join(rows)))
```

The replications use legacy CRSP (SIZ), the format available when BEM wrote the book.
The local legacy exports are newer than their original snapshot.
The newer CIZ files use different return conventions, including the timing of dividend reinvestment.
See [CRSP's comparison of the formats](https://www.crsp.org/crsp_pdf/crsp-us-stock-indexes-databases-siz-to-ciz-executive-summary/).

### Create the Parquet repository {#sec-create-data-repository}

[]{#create-data-repository}Copy `.env.example` to `.env` in the book checkout and set `DATA_DIR` to your Parquet root and `WRDS_ID` to your WRDS username.
After `uv sync`, run the setup script from that checkout.
If you already have the source files there, you can skip this step.
If your WRDS account lacks access to the legacy CRSP tables, use licensed SIZ extracts at the corresponding paths.

```sh
uv run scripts/download_wrds_tables.py
```

The following Python example shows how the script uses `db2pq.wrds_update_pq()` to export the WRDS tables to `DATA_DIR`.

```python
from db2pq import wrds_update_pq
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

tables = {
    "crsp": ["msf", "dsf", "msenames", "msedelist", "msi", "ccmxpf_lnkused"],
    "comp": ["funda"],
    "ff": ["factors_monthly", "factors_daily"],
}

for schema, names in tables.items():
    for name in names:
        wrds_update_pq(name, schema)
```

### Other inputs {#other-inputs}

Chapters [-@sec-bem-beta], [-@sec-size-replication], and [-@sec-value-replication] can export the local Parquet tables `eap.betas`, `eap.sizes`, and `eap.book_to_market`.
The annual methods chapters use the December observations from those tables.
The [render instructions](https://github.com/iangow/asset_pricing_polars#render) show how to build them.

Chapters [-@sec-bem-crsp], [-@sec-size-replication], and [-@sec-value-replication] use the [BLS all-items CPI for urban consumers, not seasonally adjusted](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCNS), from FRED, to express market capitalizations in December 2012 dollars.
This file does not come from WRDS.

## Winsorization and Truncation

**Winsorization** caps values outside chosen percentile cutoffs at the corresponding cutoff.
**Truncation** sets those values to missing, so analyses that require the variable exclude those observations.
In [Section 1.2](https://catalogimages.wiley.com/images/db/pdf/9781118095041.excerpt.pdf), @bali2016 describe both methods as ways to limit the influence of extreme values.
They suggest capping observations that still convey information about genuinely high or low values, and consider truncation when the extremes appear to come from a different process.
They urge caution when the conclusions depend on which treatment is used.

BEM compute the cutoffs separately for each year or month because they analyze each period's cross-section before summarizing the results over time.
Their 0.5% rule uses the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles.
In @sec-bem-correlation, both variables are winsorized for Pearson correlations, and Spearman correlations use ranks of the original values.
In @sec-bem-annual-fm, the regressors are winsorized and the excess-return outcome is used as observed.

We compute the winsorization cutoffs by linear interpolation with `.era.winsorize(prob=0.005, quantile_method="linear")`.
The `eap_pl.winsorized_corr()` helper applies this rule to each variable after keeping pairs with two finite values.
In @sec-bem-beta, `.over("month")` computes cutoffs separately for each month's beta estimates.
We then fit the Fama–MacBeth regressions with `statspai.fama_macbeth()`.

For examples using `.era.winsorize()` and `.era.truncate()` and a comparison with robust regression, see [Chapter 24 of *Empirical Research in Accounting*](https://iangow.github.io/era_pl_book/extreme-vals.html#sec-leone).
